data.summary: The 16‑week plan front‑loads Units 1 and 2 to address the student’s weak areas, then moves through the remaining units in a logical sequence while keeping each week to 4 hours. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to consolidate knowledge and build test stamina.

weeks.focus: Begin Unit 1 – foundational concepts of moles and atomic structure.
tasks: Do 10 practice problems on calculating moles and molar mass; check answers with the solution key.
Create a concept map linking atomic number, electron configuration, and periodic trends.

weeks.focus: Continue Unit 1 – spectroscopy and composition of mixtures.
tasks: Watch a short video on mass spectroscopy; then label a sample spectrum.
Complete 8 free‑response questions on elemental composition of pure substances and mixtures.

weeks.focus: Finish Unit 1 – periodic trends and valence concepts.
tasks: Fill out a periodic trends table (atomic radius, ionization energy, electronegativity).
Do 12 FRQ items on predicting ionic compounds from valence electron patterns.

weeks.focus: Start Unit 2 – bond types and intramolecular forces.
tasks: Draw and label covalent, ionic, and metallic bonds for given formulas.
Solve 6 problems calculating bond energy changes using potential energy curves.

weeks.focus: Unit 1 review & reinforce concepts through live class.
tasks: Participate in Class 9300 and take notes on any misconceptions.
After class, redo 5 class examples without looking at notes.
Complete a timed set of 5 FRQs covering moles, spectroscopy, and composition.

weeks.focus: Continue Unit 2 – structures of solids and metals.
tasks: Sketch lattice structures for ionic solids and metallic alloys.
Answer 8 FRQs comparing properties of ionic vs metallic solids.

weeks.focus: Unit 2 – Lewis structures, resonance, and formal charge.
tasks: Draw Lewis diagrams for 10 molecules, indicating formal charges.
Complete 6 resonance‑structure problems and justify the major contributor.

weeks.focus: Unit 2 – VSEPR & hybridization, reinforced by live class.
tasks: Attend Class 9301; focus on VSEPR predictions.
After class, predict shapes for 8 new molecules and compare with answer key.
Do a 10‑minute timed quiz on Lewis diagrams, resonance, and VSEPR.

weeks.focus: Unit 3 – intermolecular forces and states of matter.
tasks: Create a table of IMFs for solids, liquids, gases; include examples.
Solve 7 problems on phase changes using the kinetic molecular theory.

weeks.focus: Unit 3 – gases and ideal gas law.
tasks: Complete 12 practice calculations using PV=nRT and kinetic theory relationships.
Do a set of 5 FRQs that require converting between units and applying the ideal gas law.
Balance 10 chemical equations, including net ionic forms.
Perform stoichiometry calculations for 8 reaction scenarios.

weeks.focus: Unit 5 – reaction rates and rate laws.
tasks: Plot concentration vs. time graphs for first‑order reactions.
Write rate laws for 6 given reactions and determine the rate‑determining step.

weeks.focus: Unit 5 – elementary reactions and concentration changes.
tasks: Solve 9 problems on integrated rate laws for zero, first, and second order.
Identify elementary steps in 5 complex mechanisms.
Calculate enthalpy changes for 7 reactions using Hess’s law.
Interpret energy diagrams for exothermic and endothermic processes.
Take a 45‑minute timed practice set covering at least one question from each listed unit.
Review each missed question, rewrite the solution, and note the underlying concept.
Complete a full‑length AP Chemistry practice exam (timed).
Analyze results, focusing on any remaining weak spots; create a quick‑reference sheet for formulas.

data.final_week_advice: In the final week, simulate test conditions: work in a quiet space, use only allowed calculators, and stick to the 3‑hour exam limit. After the practice exam, spend the remaining time reviewing errors, reinforcing key equations, and practicing quick recall of concepts. Stay confident and trust the systematic preparation you’ve built over the past 16 weeks.
